newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech group wins tender for Prague clearing house.
newsitem.headline: Czech group wins tender for Prague clearing house.

text.p: A Czech consortium comprising firms connected to the country's two bourses and the Central Securities Registry has won a finance ministry tender to set up and manage a unified securities clearing house, the director of one of the winners, RM-System told Reuters on Thursday.

Lubomir Sticha said the winning group included the state-run Central Securities Registry (SCP), the Prague Stock Exchange's clearing unit Univyc, computer technology firm PVT a.s. and its subsidiary, the retail securities bourse RM-System.
Soon after Sticha's comment, Finance Ministry spokeswoman Ludmila Nutilova confirmed that the group had been chosen over a Czech group called "Bull".
"There is a joint agreement between the firm Univyc, the Prague Stock Exchange, PVT, and RM-S (to set up the clearing house)," Nutilova said.
The finance ministry earlier this year launched an intiative to try to streamline the Czech securities settlement process which did not permit a direct delivery-versus-payment system.
Under the current system, payment for trades is settled with the central bank, while the actual transfer of shares is settled by the SCP.
The new clearing house, which is scheduled to begin test operation by the end of October and actual operation by the beginning of next year, is expected to unify the process.
